question.problem:
$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨\text{_____},\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,6\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ)$ above parametrizes the ellipsoid defined in Cartesian coordinates as $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{16}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{36}=1.$ What is the first component of $f?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we make the following substitution:

$$
x=2X,\,y=4Y,\,z=6Z
$$

Substituting the above into the Cartesian equation of our ellipsoid, we get

$$
{X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}+{Z}^{2}=1,
$$

which is the equation of a sphere of radius $1$ centered at the origin in $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates.
In spherical polar coordinates, this sphere has the equation $\rho =1.$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical polar coordinates of a point, then its $(X,Y,Z)$ coordinates can be found using the following formulas:

$$
X=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,Y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,Z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨2X,4Y,6Z⟩ \\  & =⟨2\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,4\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,6\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨2\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,4\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,6\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,6\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ and $ϕ\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$
